panels.title: Experiment context — select a report's time-window link
panels.description: Run identifiers live in annotations and reports, never metric labels. App filters do not filter host-wide or campaign-wide panels.

panels.title: 1 · LATENCY — successful requests and failures measured separately
Successful read latency — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Replica histogram buckets are summed before computing percentiles. Normal and degraded contracts are provisional settings in benchmarks/slo.json.

panels.title: Successful writes and orders — p95 / p99
Failed requests — p95
panels.description: 409 order conflicts are expected business rejections, not availability failures.

panels.title: DB operation latency — p95
panels.description: Operation time includes pool waiting and any configured synthetic delay; it is not pure PostgreSQL execution time.

panels.title: Redis command latency — p95
panels.description: Includes connection establishment, Redis wait, and timeout. Correlate with Redis exporter and container metrics.

panels.title: Client read latency — window p95 / p99
panels.description: k6 native histograms permit windowed quantiles; raw compressed samples are retained for exact fault-window analysis.

panels.title: 2 · TRAFFIC — offered, achieved, successful, and avoided work
Cache hits by layer / DB loader origins
panels.description: Request and write-through refresh loads are separate. Cache lookup counts include protected-mode polling; they are not a request hit ratio.

panels.title: Layer-specific lookup hit ratios
panels.description: No denominator means unknown. L1 hits do not enter the L2 denominator. Errors/invalid values are shown in the error panels.

panels.title: Dropped iterations / second
panels.description: Absent drop counters are interpreted as zero only while iteration counter samples exist. Missing generator samples remain unknown.

panels.title: 3 · ERRORS — unexpected failures, expected rejections, and degradation
Unexpected HTTP error ratio
panels.description: Excludes health probes and expected 409 order conflicts. Includes unexpected client and server errors; a zero denominator is unknown.

panels.title: Fallbacks to PostgreSQL
panels.description: Fallbacks may return HTTP 200; correlate with DB saturation and latency rather than classifying them as HTTP failures.

panels.title: Fault / recovery phase error ratio
panels.description: Rolling window can straddle phase boundaries. Use saved sample timestamps for exact phase acceptance.

panels.title: 4 · SATURATION — resource limits, queues, and bottleneck evidence
Container CPU usage — cores
panels.description: Service/project selectors apply to container panels. No CPU quota means a percentage-of-quota cannot be calculated.

panels.title: Memory working set / finite limit
panels.description: Containers without a finite memory limit are omitted, not reported as unconstrained zero-percent usage.

panels.title: PostgreSQL locks not granted
panels.description: Exporter availability/version determines lock-wait coverage. Missing series are unknown.

panels.title: Host CPU busy
panels.description: Host-wide, including unrelated processes and other Compose projects.

panels.title: H1–H3 · Performance, capacity, and DB protection
Explicit SQL attempts by operation
panels.description: Excludes BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK and driver-internal queries. db_queries_total remains a logical operation counter.

panels.title: DB snapshot loads / successful reads
panels.description: Includes write-through refresh work. Compare matched throughput and write mix; this is not itself the H3 reduction versus baseline.

panels.title: H4 / H7 · Freshness observations — not a linearizability proof
Last sequential probe stale fraction
panels.description: Last E17 result, not continuously measured freshness. Missing data is unknown.

panels.title: Observed staleness / freshness budget
panels.description: Last stale observation is a lower bound. A short probe cannot establish an upper bound; never infer pass from this chart alone.

panels.title: Inventory invariant violations from runtime probe
panels.description: Only emitted by the opt-in concurrent-order test. No probe means unknown, not zero violations.

panels.title: H5–H6 · Failure recovery and stampede coordination
Refill work and follower fallback
panels.description: Use flush/expiry annotations and exact raw counters to calculate amplification per event; a rolling ratio can cross event boundaries.

panels.title: Active SLO alerts
panels.description: Rules use rolling windows and require sustained breaches. A short run may not fire an alert despite failing an acceptance threshold.

panels.title: H7–H8 · Cache layers and Redis scale-out
Shard request share
panels.description: One hot key stays on one shard. Throughput improvement alone does not prove a Redis bottleneck.

panels.title: Telemetry health — missing data is never a passing measurement
